claimB.split: held-out test split (20 charges: 13 with a true exposure, 7 with none, 5 hard). Dev split (10) used only to check the threshold.
claimB.dataset: synthetic charges authored for this project (not real customer data)
claimB.method: SQL linker: normalized descriptor + trigram/abbreviation/token name score + time window (agent confirmation not applied in this eval)
claimB.caveat: Optimistic by construction: these synthetic charges were written by the same team as the linker and every positive was checked to be solvable by it (data integrity test). Treat F1 near 1.0 as "the pipeline works", not as expected real-world accuracy. The naive baseline mainly loses on abbreviated descriptors.

claimA.split: held-out TEST split (n=91) of a seed-42, 70/30 split stratified by category (eval/messages_split.json, committed before any tuning); rules were tuned on the 215 train messages only
claimA.dataset: Bluff's own synthetic message set (bluff-synthetic-v1: 306 SMS/email messages generated with NVIDIA Nemotron, model-audited and hand-reviewed). NOT T-Mobile data; none was provided.
claimA.mode: live Nemotron agent with rules fallback (as deployed)
claimA.baseline_name: Stand-in baseline: contains a link → scam (not T-Mobile's baseline)
claimA.caveat: Synthetic data written by one model: phrasing is more uniform than real traffic, so these numbers are optimistic for real messages. The generator required scam links to use scam-prone domains and legit links to use .example, which makes link signals unusually strong here; the no-link subset below shows results without that help. Rules were written by looking at the train split (n=215), not the test split; on train the tuned rules score F1 1.00 (before: 0.70), so the drop to the test numbers is the overfitting you should expect on new messages. Small n: each test category has 3 (scam) or 5 (legit) messages, so per-category numbers are anecdotes.
claimA.headline: live

methods.note: 88/91 verdicts came from Nemotron; 3 fell back to the rules (timeout, rate limit or invalid answer)

confidence_model.formula: floor + (cap − floor) · (1 − e^(−net/tau)), net = |S − L| · √(|S − L| / (S + L)), S/L = summed scam/legit evidence weights
confidence_model.note: Unsure verdicts claim nothing and are left out of the calibration buckets.

live.pacing: calls paced 1600 ms apart (trial-key rate limit), so latency includes queueing
